title: pi-telegram-tts sub-block (v0.3.0)
description:
Per-provider TTS sub-block inside `telegram.json#extensions["pi-telegram-tts"]`. The v0.3.0 design lets every CLI arg the bundled tts-*.mjs scripts support be reachable from this JSON object — no template editing required. The provider writes the sub-block (with v0.1.0 top-level `voice` / `model` as fallbacks) to a tempfile and passes `--config <path>` to the script. Resolution order per field: sub-block field > top-level field > script's hardcoded DEFAULTS. Live edits take effect on the next voice-tagged turn (the provider re-reads config on every call, no restart needed).

The schema is the canonical reference for the v0.3.0 surface and is consumed by:
  - VS Code / IntelliJ for inline validation when the user adds `"$schema": "..."` to telegram.json
  - (v0.6.0:) the operator or agent edits `telegram.json` directly via filesystem tools; the 200ms hot-reload watcher picks up the change. There is no longer a form-driven UI or an in-package config writer — the agent's own `read`/`write` tools are the canonical surface.

Version: 1 (no migration needed; the v0.3.0 reader accepts all earlier shapes).

disabled.description: Master switch. When true, the provider returns `undefined` and the bridge falls through to `outboundHandlers[0].template`. The operator or agent edits this directly in `telegram.json`; the 200ms hot-reload watcher picks up the change on the next voice-tagged turn.

provider.description: Which TTS script to spawn. `minimax` → `tts-minimax.mjs` (bundled); `openai` → `tts-openai.mjs` (bundled). When unset, the provider falls through to the template (the v0.1.0 default).

voice.description: Top-level voice fallback (v0.1.0). Used by the script only when the active provider's sub-block has no `voice` field. v0.4.0 will mark this as `> Deprecated: use the per-provider sub-block instead`; will be removed in v1.0. Defaults to the script's DEFAULTS (`Cantonese_CuteGirl` for MiniMax, `coral` for OpenAI) when omitted.

model.description: Top-level model fallback (v0.1.0). Same deprecation as `voice`. Defaults to the script's DEFAULTS (`speech-2.8-hd` for MiniMax, `gpt-4o-mini-tts` for OpenAI) when omitted.

composeWithText.description: v0.4.0: text+voice composition. `"off"` (default) sends voice only. `"auto"` sends a text message with the same content as the voice, then the voice follows. This is the v0.1.0 `voice.sendTranscript: true` behavior, reimplemented at the extension level because upstream `@llblab/pi-telegram@0.38.0` removed the bridge-owned `sendTranscript` config + the `getTelegramVoiceSendTranscript()` helper + the provider-returned `transcriptText` field. The text is sent via `sendTelegramView({ text, parseMode: "html" }, { scope: { kind: "active-turn" } })` just before the bridge uploads the OGG, so the user sees text first, then voice. The v0.1.0 "voice with caption" UX (single message, text+voice in the same frame) is no longer achievable via the public upstream API. Best-effort: a `sendTelegramView` failure is logged + recorded as a runtime event, and the voice is still delivered.

minimaxBlock.description: Per-provider sub-block for the MiniMax T2A HTTP API. Every field here maps to a CLI flag in `tts-minimax.mjs` (the v0.3.0 path-mapping hotfix ensures `--config` keys get the same path remap as the CLI flags). Nested fields like `voice_setting.voice_id` and `audio_setting.sample_rate` are accepted as nested-object form (`{"voice_setting": {"voice_id": "X"}}`) for power users, but the flat form (`{"voice": "X"}`) is the recommended shape and what the path-mapping remap handles. Omit any field to fall back to the script's DEFAULTS.

voice.description: Voice ID. Path: `voice_setting.voice_id`. DEFAULTS: `Cantonese_CuteGirl`. The MiniMax T2A API voice catalog is documented at https://platform.minimaxi.com/docs/api-reference/speech-t2a-http. **Live-tested:** `Cantonese_PlayfulMan` works (the user's choice); `Cantonese_CuteGirl` is the script default.

model.description: Model ID. Path: `model`. DEFAULTS: `speech-2.8-hd`. `speech-2.8-hd` is the high-def Cantonese-friendly default; `speech-2.6-hd` and the `speech-2.x-turbo` variants trade quality for speed; `speech-01` / `speech-02` legacy have a 480-char per-chunk limit.

lang.description: Language boost. Path: `language_boost`. DEFAULTS: `Chinese,Yue`. Format: `Language,Dialect` (e.g. `Chinese,Yue` for Cantonese, `English,American` for en-US, `Chinese,Mandarin` for Mandarin).

speed.description: Speech rate. Path: `voice_setting.speed`. DEFAULTS: `1`. 0.5 = half-speed, 2.0 = double-speed. **Live-tested:** 1.3 / 1.5 / 1.6 all audibly faster than 1.0.

vol.description: Volume. Path: `voice_setting.vol`. DEFAULTS: `1`. 0.1 = nearly silent, 10.0 = max.

pitch.description: Voice-setting pitch shift (semitones). Path: `voice_setting.pitch`. DEFAULTS: `0`. Distinct from `voice_modify.pitch` (which has range -100..100 and a different effect).

emotion.description: Emotional affect. Path: `voice_setting.emotion`. Available on the `speech-2.x-hd` / `speech-2.x-turbo` model families (not on the `speech-01` / `speech-02` legacy). **Live-tested:** `happy` audibly different from neutral.

text_normalization.description: Enable text normalization (expand numbers, abbreviations). Path: `voice_setting.text_normalization`. Set to `false` to read symbols literally.

latex_read.description: Enable LaTeX reading mode. Path: `voice_setting.latex_read`. When true, the model pronounces LaTeX formulas. Default off.

sample_rate.description: Output sample rate. Path: `audio_setting.sample_rate`. DEFAULTS: `32000`. The `tts-*.mjs` writes an MP3/OGG at this rate; the bridge's ffmpeg wrap re-encodes to OGG/Opus 48kHz for Telegram regardless. **Live-tested:** 44100 vs 24000 had audible quality difference.

bitrate.description: Output bitrate (kbps). Path: `audio_setting.bitrate`. DEFAULTS: `128000`. Higher = better quality, larger file.

format.description: Output audio format. Path: `audio_setting.format`. DEFAULTS: `mp3`. The ffmpeg wrap transcodes whatever the script produces to OGG/Opus for Telegram, so the choice mostly affects the intermediate file size.

channel.description: Output channel count. Path: `audio_setting.channel`. DEFAULTS: `1` (mono). Set to `2` for stereo. **Live-tested:** `2` produces a stereo OGG.

force_cbr.description: Force constant bitrate encoding. Path: `audio_setting.force_cbr`. Default false (VBR).

modify_pitch.description: Voice-modify pitch shift. Path: `voice_modify.pitch`. DEFAULTS: `0`. Distinct from `voice_setting.pitch` (which has range -12..12 and a different effect).

sound_effects.description: Audio effect applied to the output. Path: `voice_modify.sound_effects`. DEFAULTS: none. **Live-tested:** `spacious_echo` and `auditorium_echo` audibly echo-y; differences between the two are subtle (spacious = small room, auditorium = larger hall).

aigc_watermark.description: Embed the AIGC watermark in the audio. Path: `aigc_watermark` (top-level). DEFAULTS: `true` (the script's NEGATIVE_FLAGS table covers `--no-watermark`). Set to `false` to opt out.

apply_text_filter.description: Apply the platform's text filter. Path: `apply_text_filter` (top-level). DEFAULTS: `true`. Set to `false` to send raw text to the model.

subtitle_enable.description: Include subtitle metadata in the response. Path: `subtitle_enable` (top-level). DEFAULTS: `false`. If true, set `subtitle_type` to `word` or `sentence`.

subtitle_type.description: Subtitle granularity. Path: `subtitle_type` (top-level). Only meaningful when `subtitle_enable: true`. DEFAULTS: `word`.

emoji_event.description: Enable emoji-event triggers in the synthesized audio. Path: `emoji_event` (top-level). DEFAULTS: `false`.

output_format.description: Response format for the audio bytes. Path: `output_format` (top-level). DEFAULTS: `hex`. The bridge expects `hex`; the script handles the conversion. Don't change unless you know what you're doing.

stream.description: Use streaming response. Path: `stream` (top-level). The script refuses to use this — `tts-minimax.mjs:416-421` exits 2 with a clear error if `stream: true` is set, because the SSE response format is incompatible with the script's JSON parser. Leave false.

pronunciation_dict.description: Custom pronunciation hints. Path: `pronunciation_dict` (top-level). DEFAULTS: unset. **Format:** `{"tone": ["word/pronunciation", "word2/pronunciation2"]}` — the `tone` array contains slash-separated `word/pronunciation` pairs. **Live-tested:** setting `tone: ["example/pronunciation"]` produced 4 beeps at the end of the audio (the API tried to apply the dummy hint and produced artifact). Only set this with real pronunciation hints. To disable, omit the field entirely.

items.description: Slash-separated word/pronunciation pair (e.g. "GIF/gif" to force a hard G).

timbre_weights.description: Voice blending — produce a hybrid voice by mixing several. Path: `timbre_weights` (top-level). DEFAULTS: unset. Each element is `{"voice_id": "X", "weight": N}`. **NOT live-tested** in v0.3.0.

openaiBlock.description: Per-provider sub-block for the OpenAI `/v1/audio/speech` API. OpenAI's body is flat (no nesting), so all fields here are top-level in the script's request body. The script's `--config` path-mapping is a no-op for these (flat schema) but the consistency is intentional — both scripts apply the same remap, so any future OpenAI nested field would Just Work.

voice.description: Voice ID. Path: `voice` (top-level in the API body). DEFAULTS: `coral`. The 4 voices not in `tts-1` / `tts-1-hd` are: ballad, cedar, marin, verse (gpt-4o-mini-tts only).

model.description: Model ID. Path: `model`. DEFAULTS: `gpt-4o-mini-tts`. `tts-1` and `tts-1-hd` are the older models; `gpt-4o-mini-tts` supports the `instructions` field.

instructions.description: Style/tone prompt. Path: `instructions` (top-level in the API body). Only sent if the model supports it (gpt-4o-mini-tts). DEFAULTS: unset (no instructions field is sent, which biases the output less than a generic prompt). **Live-tested:** `"Speak in Cantonese."` produced a coral voice that attempted Cantonese pronunciation (the underlying model still speaks English-leaning but with intonation cues).

speed.description: Speech rate. Path: `speed`. DEFAULTS: `1.0`. 0.25 = quarter-speed, 4.0 = quadruple-speed.

response_format.description: Output format. Path: `response_format`. DEFAULTS: `mp3`. The ffmpeg wrap transcodes to OGG/Opus regardless.
